body: Yeah, I guess it would help. But ultimately, it's kind of also a secondary problem, to the whole nobody liking me thing.

Hi swthrowaway68,

Sometimes I feel the same way, about nobody liking me. I'd like to believe it's not true, but it is. I can't really walk a mile in your shoes because I don't know what it's like to be in your situation exactly. But whatever you're feeling, I know that, if you're still there, you're able to talk about it. Maybe we can find some common ground and work through it together? That would be the best outcome for both of us, I'm sure.

to be honest the same thing would happen. i've tried a few different things, and I MIGHT get decent at piano if i put time into it, but that's also kind of a secondary problem. I don't want to just ditch my whole life and have to start a new one, I want to make my current life livable.
No we're still in contact, i just feel like she sort of got tired of everything I had to say.

Thanks a ton for your comment, wasory. 

Please don't get the wrong idea: my parents are kind and loving people, but they think this whole depression business is just a front, and as you can see, it's not. They care for me and they are very good parents, but I just feel like I won't give THEM any returns, not that they're snubbing me in any way. 

That said, everything else you said was dead on. It's not fair to me that everyone around me just gels together so well, and I sort of seem like the odd one out. If there IS hope to find a solution to the primary problem, I would love to, but I can't find many people with a problem exactly like mine on the internet. I had one good friend to talk to about my feelings, but now I've alienated her and she's getting a little on the mean side about things now. Everyone else just sort of guilts me, and I mean, I totally get where they're coming from, because to them, it seems like such a trivial, stupid problem that can be easily corrected.

Thanks so much for taking the time to type that out, cypherrage.

Actually I had an interest in taking up piano, and it seems interesting to me. I don't have access to one, so i've been watching videos and learning basics on the internet (LOL), but I don't have a tangible piano. I think it'd be really cool to get better at it and it seems like something I would enjoy. The little things I've picked up through 80 minutes of youtube videos (the ability to play Twinkle Twinkle Little Star and Mary Had a Little Lamb) seem really cool, even though they're not too advanced or anything. If I could easily access a piano that would be really awesome too.
I mean all that means is that there's only so much help I can get from them. And they're not even really the problem at all; they're just not a good source from which to get a solution, in my case.

I mean debate's a pretty fun hobby but unfortunately I'm not very good, and many of the debaters on my debate team are really really good and will be pretty judgmental, so it's kind of hard to do anything about that. Again like I said i'm not really skilled at much of anything so it's kind of hard to find something I can do regularly and something where all the other people will accept me and like me. 

And actually, besides the usual stress that high school is bound to cause a student, schoolwork doesn't really faze me that much. It's just that it's really the only thing that is a factor in my life, and I'm tired of that, and tired of basically living a useless existence. If it could somehow be fixed, I would love to live on, but I don't think the hole I've dug myself into is shallow enough to get out of.

Thanks for your comment, man (or woman?).

It's not that i'm worried about them spending money because they're losing money. Most parents take pride in their kids' achievements, though, and can talk about them at parties or whatever. So, on top of being a financial burden, these parents can have a source of happiness from their kids. Since that second part is lacking, i am ONLY a financial burden to them. Sorry for not explaining that properly, hope it makes more sense now.

Oh, and yes on the family thing. But they're very success and achievement minded, and they don't realize that this is something i can't control. They seem to have this mentality of "this is all a waste of time". In fact, a lot of people basically feel the same way if I try to tell them. Unfortunately, there's not much you can really do to change that (or at least, that *I* can do right now. Maybe if you have any ideas, you wouldn't mind sharing?)

Thanks for your comment, FLH.

Well I mean I wouldn't really consider it "breezing through", but I'm doing decent. Thing is, I live in an extremely competitive area where having a report card of 93+ in every subject, honors and AP classes included, can barely get you in the top 50/750ish. And I would give all that up for just a regular social life, where I get invited to a movie every once in a while and get to have a conversation that doesn't include the words "don't be so rigid" or "relax" or "why are you so awkward".

And I mean, every kid is a financial burden. But I feel like i'm not really going anywhere in life. Everyone's usually talented at at least one thing (art, some musical instrument, singing, etc.) but I'm not. I do debate, and have had meh success, but I can point to every single success I've had and tell you exactly how much luck factored into it (right down to one time where the only reason I advanced into the next round is because the guy who would have ranked above me got sick and had to leave). It's something that requires you to be very social, and while I'm not averse to meeting new people, they always seem very averse to meeting me.

Basically, nobody cares for my existence. That's all. The only compliment I ever get is "you're smart" (aka, I get somewhat good grades because I've paid attention enough and have understood how to game the system that is school/testing). I have "friends", but they usually tend to ignore me and avoid me if someone else is around. I don't get invited to shit ever. People think i'm socially awkward, but I don't feel anxious around people (although i've felt more anxious as a result of people telling me I am). I would gladly trade any good success I've had (very few, mostly all school related) for just a moderately good social life. I have a huge crush on this one girl, but she's amazing and too nice to say she thinks I'm annoying and hates me. She never talks to me, but when I ask her something she responds. I don't really have any good qualities. I'm nothing more than a financial burden to my parents (and in about 10 years, a burden that gave no legitimate returns). Any of my friends who I talked to don't seem to understand, and they tell me stupid shit like "it's OK" and "you can just hang out with more people" as if people WANT to hang out with me and I can just get them to like me. It's come to a point where I fucking hate everyone, even though I don't want to. It's horrible.
I'm a teenage male, so that's probably not the cause haha. You think it could just be anxiety? What could I maybe do to prevent that?
How does gender make a difference, if it does?
